explanation: Proposed: raise server-1-cover another 0.20 m and shift it 0.35 m left (−X); pull server-1 forward 0.20 m (+Z); raise the entire fan wall 0.12 m (+Y) relative to the chassis. Only these three local transforms change; fan children retain their hierarchy and local transforms, and all server children inherit the server's forward movement. In normal assembled operation, CPU heat sinks conduct processor heat into their bases and fins, whose large surface area transfers heat to air. The fan wall drives front-to-rear airflow through the fin channels and carries warmed air out the rear. The cover and airflow guides help prevent air bypassing the heat sinks. The proposed separation is a teaching view, not an operating configuration.
prompt: Lift server-1-cover another 0.20 meters and move it 0.35 meters to the left. Pull server-1 forward by 0.20 meters. Separate the entire server-1-fan-wall upward by 0.12 meters, preserving its fan children. Explain how the fan wall and CPU heat sinks work together. Keep every other existing local transform unchanged.
